The skill journey, step by step#

This is the loop the alpha supports end to end for a skill, with each step as a page action and as an SDK call. caliber/caliber-ui/e2e/skill-journey.spec.ts drives the page steps (it creates the skill with POST /skills, the endpoint the wizard saves to, rather than filling the wizard) and caliber/tests/test_sdk_skill_journey.py drives the SDK steps, both on the shipped defaults.

#StepIn the page (Skills)In the SDKWhat you should see
1AuthorBuild Skill, then fill the wizard; or open a skill and edit it on the Author stageskills.create(name, content=..., owner=...)version 1 in the version history
2PreviewRender Preview: enter variables as JSON, Render Skillskills.render(skill_id, variables={...})the content with variables filled in, and any left unresolved
3Check selectionTrigger Tests: Check selection for one message, or build cases on Scenario Sets and run them all from Trigger Testsskills.test_selection(skill_id, query)whether the skill would be chosen, with a score and a reason
4CalibrateRuns: Calibrateskills.calibrate(skill_id)"Calibration queued", then a run under Calibration runs
5ReviewRuns: Review & apply on a run at candidate_readyjobs.wait(job_id), then read job.candidate and job.eval_resultsthe diff, the baseline, candidate and change scores, the gate result, and a banner when the evaluation is simulated
6ApplyApply to skill (disabled when the evaluation gate failed)jobs.apply(job_id)the skill is now the candidate, as the next version
7Roll backAuthor: Roll back on the live version in the version historyskills.rollback(skill_id)the earlier content is current again, as a new version

Three things to know before you trust the result.

  • Skill evidence is not measured by default. A skill calibration has no test set. With the default fake providers the scores are canned and the run says so: the review shows "Simulated evaluation — not evidence" and 0 evaluation examples, and job.eval_results["simulated"] is true. Apply anyway only if you have judged the diff yourself.
  • Rolling back never rewrites history. A skill is one row with a version counter, so rolling back restores the earlier content as a new version. After apply and rollback you have versions 1, 2 and 3, and version 3 has the same text as version 1.
  • Roles decide who can do what. Anyone in the project can read, render and preview. Recording runs and baselines needs reviewer or above, calibrating needs reviewer or above, and applying a candidate needs editor or owner. Creating, importing and binding a skill also need editor or owner (plus the global caliber.operator scope). Changing a skill's content directly, and rolling it back, also need the global caliber.admin scope. A member whose role is too weak gets a permission error (403), and a person outside the project sees "not found" (404) for every one of these. See Auth and project scoping.

1. What skills are for in CALIBER#

Skills are reusable instruction assets. They let you keep repeatable behavioral guidance separate from the rest of the workflow or assistant logic.
